assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale measurement of intergenerational mobility has transformed a central question in public and labour economics into a tractable empirical research programme.
assessment.attribution: Chetty and Hendren are central to the measurement and place-based mobility agenda, with Friedman an important collaborator in its development.
assessment.maturity: The programme has generated a large, durable literature and policy-relevant evidence across settings.
uncertainties: The long credited list makes the appropriate laureate set contestable.
Interpretation of place effects remains methodologically demanding.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work changed understanding of how technology and trade reshape local labour markets, tasks, wages and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn and Hanson form a coherent core for the task and trade-shock evidence; Katz is also an important intellectual contributor.
assessment.maturity: Its empirical designs, findings and implications have been extensively tested and remain central to labour economics.
uncertainties: The relative weight of trade versus technology mechanisms varies across contexts.
Credit allocation between the task literature and the trade-shock literature is not straightforward.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The modern analysis of monopsony supplied a powerful framework for interpreting wage setting and many labour-market institutions.
assessment.attribution: Manning is the clearest individual intellectual anchor among the listed candidates, while the empirical expansion of the field has many contributors.
assessment.maturity: The framework has become highly influential and has received substantial empirical support.
uncertainties: The listed discovery combines foundational theory with a wider empirical literature not readily captured by one name.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Correspondence and audit designs provided unusually transparent evidence on labour-market discrimination and redirected empirical work in the area.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand and Mullainathan are especially closely associated with a landmark correspondence-study contribution; Charles is an important scholar in the broader field.
assessment.maturity: The approach has been replicated widely and has had enduring scientific and public significance.
uncertainties: Audit studies identify particular margins of discrimination and do not by themselves measure all discriminatory mechanisms.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on early-life conditions, health and skill formation has established the economic importance of childhood circumstances across the life cycle.
assessment.attribution: Currie, Almond and Cunha represent complementary empirical and structural contributions to a coherent field.
assessment.maturity: The evidence base and its influence on education, health and social-policy research are extensive.
uncertainties: The discovery description spans distinct mechanisms and methodological traditions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification made credible empirical conclusions possible where point identification depends on unpersuasive assumptions.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the foundational figure; Tamer and Molinari made major extensions and applications.
assessment.maturity: The ideas are mature, broadly used in econometrics and especially valuable for disciplined policy evaluation.
uncertainties: Its influence is more methodological than readily visible in a single applied discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The empirical study of taxable-income responses and optimal income taxation materially improved the evidence base for tax design.
assessment.attribution: Saez is central to the modern synthesis, with Chetty providing major work on behavioural responses; Slemrod and Stantcheva are also consequential contributors.
assessment.maturity: The framework is well established and has reshaped research and policy discussion.
uncertainties: Elasticities and welfare conclusions remain sensitive to institutional setting and assumptions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantile regression fundamentally expanded empirical economics beyond conditional means and enabled systematic distributional analysis.
assessment.attribution: Koenker and Bassett are the unmistakable originators; Chernozhukov made major subsequent advances.
assessment.maturity: The method is long-established, broadly applicable and deeply integrated into econometric practice.
uncertainties: Its exceptional methodological importance may be less readily framed as a discrete economic discovery.
